RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Emerson Hayes
Member ID: W807153430
Reference Number: POC-9668BA39E4-60948
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-04
Requested Service/CPT: Knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy, CPT 29881

To the Appeals & Grievances Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29881 (arthroscopic knee meniscectomy), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-04. The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree, and I ask that this denial be reversed based on the clinical record summarized below.

1. The record does document an extensive trial of conservative treatment.

My symptoms have been present for approximately 12 months, with progressive pain unrelieved by rest. During that time I completed:
- Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion: 14 weeks, from 2026-03-30 to 2026-07-06, totaling 24 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
- NSAID therapy for 6 months, with inadequate relief;
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-23, which provided only 2 weeks of partial relief.

This course of treatment — physical therapy, pharmacologic management, and an injection — exceeds the general conservative-care benchmark referenced in the plan's own knee arthroscopy prior-authorization guidance, which I understand states that meniscal tears generally require: "Failure of at least 6 weeks of non-operative treatment, including at least two of the following: o Rest or activity modifications/limitations o Ice/heat o Protected weight bearing o Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol o Brace/orthosis o Physical therapy modalities o Supervised home exercise o Weight optimization o Corticosteroid injection." [Source: Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet, summarizing Evolent Clinical Guideline for Knee Arthroscopy (referenced as CG-316/CG-1764), the criteria set applied by the plan's musculoskeletal surgery vendor, Evolent, to knee arthroscopy/meniscectomy prior authorization requests.] My 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy, 6 months of NSAID therapy, and a corticosteroid injection more than satisfy this standard, both in duration and in number/type of modalities used.

2. My clinical presentation independently qualifies for an exception to the conservative-treatment requirement.

The same guidance describes specific circumstances in which "Non-operative treatment for meniscal tears is not required," including: "History of acute injury/onset of symptoms with a locked knee and/or mechanical symptoms of locking; Physical examination demonstrates ANY positive meniscal findings on examination or demonstrates evidence of a locked knee (loss of terminal extension); MRI demonstrates a bucket-handle tear of the meniscus. (Does not include an extruded meniscus or flap tears)." [Same source as above.]

My MRI of 2026-05-24 documents a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. My examination findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side, and I experience locking and giving way, with inability to squat or kneel and function limited to level walking. This presentation appears to meet the description of the exception quoted above, meaning that under the plan's own stated criteria, a lengthy additional trial of conservative treatment should not be required as a precondition for authorization — independent of the substantial conservative treatment I have already completed.

3. My imaging findings meet the arthritis-severity threshold referenced for meniscal procedures.

The same source states: "Unless the patient has a locked knee with a displaced bucket-handle tear, weight-bearing X-rays must show no more than mild arthritis for approval of meniscus procedures. (No more than K-L 2 changes – see grading appendix*)." My MRI of 2026-05-24 documents preserved articular cartilage with a Kellgren-Lawrence grade of 1, which is well within the "no more than mild arthritis" threshold — and, as noted above, my presentation also independently falls under the locked-knee/bucket-handle-tear exception.

4. Additional factors supporting medical necessity.

I have no active local or systemic infection and no untreated substance use disorder. My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti (orthopedic surgery), has determined that arthroscopic meniscectomy is medically necessary in light of the mechanical locking, functional limitation, and failure of conservative measures to provide durable relief.

Requested action

Based on the documentation above, I ask that Harvard Pilgrim reverse the denial of CPT 29881 and approve the requested arthroscopic knee meniscectomy as medically necessary.

I have enclosed/am requesting that my provider submit the following supporting documentation:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-30 to 2026-07-06, 24 visits)
- Medication and injection records, including the 2026-04-23 corticosteroid injection note
- MRI report dated 2026-05-24
- Office visit/examination notes documenting locking, giving way, and provocative testing
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Marchetti

Note on quoted material: The passages above in quotation marks are quoted verbatim from the Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet, a document Evolent (the vendor Harvard Pilgrim uses to administer prior authorization for knee arthroscopy/meniscectomy) publishes to summarize its Knee Arthroscopy clinical guideline. I have not been able to obtain and verify every line of the full, currently-in-force edition of that underlying guideline (the complete multi-page document); I am relying on the tip-sheet language as the best available statement of the criteria the plan applies, and I ask that Harvard Pilgrim confirm which specific edition and section of the guideline was applied to my request and provide me with a full copy of it, as I am entitled to under the plan's Medical Necessity Guidelines disclosure process.

I request written confirmation of receipt of this appeal and a decision within the timeframe required under Massachusetts law and my plan's appeal procedures. If any additional information is needed to complete this review, please contact me at the phone number or email above, or contact Dr. Marchetti's office at [provider office phone/fax].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Emerson Hayes
Member ID: W807153430
